title: THE LAY OF THE LAND

coordinateSystem.z: meters/local vertical reference; omitted until authored

rule: This map is the canonical spatial index. Every scene, recording, image job, and 3D reconstruction should reference region IDs and coordinates instead of inventing geography again.

interpretation.identityRule: Region IDs are stable. Names may change; IDs do not.
interpretation.scaleRule: Body-relative measurements inherit from the current world baseline.
interpretation.continuityRule: A recording packet references existing places and records deltas rather than replacing the world.

routeNotes.title: THE DOOR REMEMBERS
routeNotes.text: A new encounter illuminates an older node that had been waiting for it.

routeNotes.title: MASS BECOMES WEATHER
routeNotes.text: Accumulation changes the scale of a room until architecture starts responding.

routeNotes.title: THE ARCHIVE OPENS A ROOM
routeNotes.text: A visual record stops being a record and becomes a place you can enter.

routeNotes.title: KISS = CONTINUITY
routeNotes.text: A relationship survives transformation because the new form still remembers the old one.

routeNotes.title: THE WORLD LEAVES A TRACE
routeNotes.text: Every visit adds a small piece of history instead of resetting the scene.

routeNotes.title: THE ROOM GETS SMALLER
routeNotes.text: Extreme girth changes perceived distance: passageways narrow, furniture crowds, and the body becomes the scale reference.

routeNotes.title: PRESSURE OF PRESENCE
routeNotes.text: A massive form is registered through footsteps, fabric tension, floor response, and the way nearby space seems compressed.

routeNotes.title: SCALE MEMORY
routeNotes.text: Once a place has adapted to a larger baseline, returning to its old proportions feels visibly wrong.

routeNotes.title: THE THRESHOLD REMEMBERS
routeNotes.text: A familiar doorway becomes a scale witness: the architecture stays still while the body changes its meaning.

routeNotes.title: THE FLOOR REPLIES
routeNotes.text: Magnitude is registered indirectly through movement, material response, sound, and the timing of footsteps.

routeNotes.title: SCALE HAS HISTORY
routeNotes.text: A new baseline does not erase the old one; rooms and routes retain evidence of what they used to fit.

routeNotes.title: THE WORLD IS BODY-RELATIVE
routeNotes.text: Passage, reach, turning, clearance, and distance are treated as relationships between a body and its environment.

routeNotes.title: THE WITNESS STAYS
routeNotes.text: An unchanged person or object provides continuity while everything around the growing subject is re-scaled.

routeNotes.title: THE HORIZON MOVES
routeNotes.text: A new threshold makes the camera retreat: room, building, district, then landscape become the measuring frame.

routeNotes.title: THE CITY LEARNS HIS NAME
routeNotes.text: At monumental scale, routes and public spaces reorganize around a recognizable person without turning him into an anonymous landmark.

routeNotes.title: THE OLD WORLD FITS NO MORE
routeNotes.text: A preserved doorway or room records the previous baseline, making the next increase feel cumulative rather than reset.

routeNotes.title: MASS WITHOUT AMNESIA
routeNotes.text: The scale becomes extraordinary; the face, gestures, chosen name, and bonds remain continuous.

routeNotes.title: THE WORLD TELLS ON ITSELF
routeNotes.text: When unrelated records repeat the same shape, the repetition becomes evidence of a law.

routeNotes.title: POETRY IS RESIDUE
routeNotes.text: An event produces something the event itself cannot contain. That remainder seeps into image, rhythm, quotation, dream, and return.

routeNotes.title: THE WITNESS CHANGES THE RECORD
routeNotes.text: A witness does not merely observe an event; remaining present gives the event a human continuity.

routeNotes.title: THE NAME SURVIVES THE SCALE
routeNotes.text: A changed body remains reachable through name, gesture, bond, place, and memory.

routeNotes.title: DEPARTURE LEAVES A SHAPE
routeNotes.text: Leaving creates an empty position that can become a promise, a route, or a return.

routeNotes.title: THE OLD WORLD BECOMES EVIDENCE
routeNotes.text: Previous baselines are not discarded. Doorways, rooms, photographs, and memories testify that another form once occupied the world.

routeNotes.title: A RELATIONSHIP HAS GEOMETRY
routeNotes.text: Proximity, distance, remaining, returning, and being recognized form a spatial grammar between people.

routeNotes.title: THE ARCHIVE CAN DREAM
routeNotes.text: When enough traces converge, the repository begins to suggest a world that was never explicitly written as a single statement.

routeNotes.title: THE BAR GYM REMEMBERS
routeNotes.text: The room stays fixed while Luke's established baseline becomes visibly larger; equipment, mirrors, and clearances become witnesses.

routeNotes.title: HYPEER BASELINE
routeNotes.text: A completed Bwomph is not a reset. The newly stabilized Luke becomes the starting point for the next cycle.

routeNotes.title: THE FACE REMAINS
routeNotes.text: Scale can change radically while Luke's recognizable identity remains the continuity anchor.

routeNotes.title: THE HOUSE KEEPS A LIGHT ON
routeNotes.text: The cedar porch offers a warm place to return to after the noise of the district.

routeNotes.title: A TABLE IS SET
routeNotes.text: A route through the kitchen turns an arrival into a shared meal without requiring an invitation speech.

routeNotes.title: THE LANTERNS COME ON
routeNotes.text: As evening gathers, the market gives the district a public room made of food, light, music, and familiar faces.

routeNotes.title: GOOD LUCK HAS WHISKERS
routeNotes.text: A cat crosses the garden path and settles in the last warm patch of sun; the city takes it as a small sign of good fortune.

routeNotes.title: THE WATER OPENS THE VIEW
routeNotes.text: A quieter path leads from the market to the reservoir, where the city can be seen without being crowded.

routeNotes.title: THE CAT KNOWS THE WAY HOME
routeNotes.text: Cats move between sheltered courtyards and familiar doorsteps, making the gardens feel connected to the neighbourhood.

routeNotes.title: THE QUAY RETURNS TO TOWN
routeNotes.text: The shoreline path leads back toward the lanterns and the evening tables.

routeNotes.title: ROOM FOR ONE MORE
routeNotes.text: A place is made at the oak table; the newcomer can join the conversation or simply eat and listen.

routeNotes.title: NORTHGATE OPENS ITS QUAD
routeNotes.text: A tree-lined avenue climbs from the reservoir into a campus of lecture halls, workshops, music rooms and green courtyards.

routeNotes.title: ROOMS ABOVE THE QUADRANGLE
routeNotes.text: The covered walk leads to a residential college where students share kitchens, common rooms, projects and the small rituals of daily life.

routeNotes.title: STRENGTH WITHOUT CONFLICT
routeNotes.text: The athletic grounds welcome students for training, swimming, recovery and companionship; physical culture is part of a balanced campus life.

routeNotes.title: THE LATE LAMPS OF NORTHGATE
routeNotes.text: A short walk from the quad reaches the oak reading hall, media archive and editing suites, where discoveries become new work.

routeNotes.title: THE DORM GARDEN PATH
routeNotes.text: A quiet path from the residential courtyard joins the Cat Gardens, where the resident cats are considered a good sign for the day.

routeNotes.title: CAMPUS AFTER HOURS
routeNotes.text: Students drift from the library to the Common Table for supper, carrying conversations from the reading rooms into the evening.
